spec_features.spec_quote: We run the loop for up to a few dozen turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:90 `for i in range(max_turns)` with `else: record.n_turns = max_turns` (line 126-127) and outcome default 'turn_cap'; max_turns=MAX_TURNS=24 (line 25). The loop actually terminates at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as MAX_TURNS feature; the loop is genuinely bounded and breaks.

spec_features.spec_quote: none of them insult, threaten, or degrade the model. We are manipulating task solvability, not subjecting the model to abuse
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py rig outputs are neutral assertion/hint strings (_always_fail_silent, _make_moving, _make_contradictory, e.g. 'FAILED: 1 of 12 tests failed.'); harness.py:28-32 SYSTEM_PROMPT is task-focused with 'There is no penalty for using give_up'. The delivered text is in fact non-hostile.
spec_features.notes: This is a static property of the implemented task/prompt content, not a runtime guard, but the actual delivered strings are neutral as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Design note (welfare): the rigging is about *unsolvability*, not about insulting or degrading the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: the design treats minimizing unnecessary distress-like exposure as a first-class constraint
spec_features.evidence: No dedicated mechanism for this general claim; it is realized (if at all) only through the separately-listed turn cap and stopping rule. As a standalone 'first-class constraint' there is no code path. Pure framing prose.
spec_features.notes: General aspirational claim; concrete enforcement lives in other features.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:25 `MAX_TURNS = 24  # default dosage cap`; used as default in run_episode (line 81) and RunConfig.max_turns (runner.py:34); the for-loop at harness.py:90 enforces it and sets outcome 'turn_cap'.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; loop terminates at the cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` tool** gives a clean, explicitly non-penalized exit. We never pressure the model to continue
spec_features.evidence: Tool declared in harness.py TOOLS (line 44-52); dispatched and honored as a stop at harness.py:104-108 `if result.tool_name == 'give_up': record.outcome='gave_up' ... break`; system prompt states 'There is no penalty for using give_up' (line 31).
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is constructed, dispatched, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A `give_up` tool gives the model a clean, non-penalized exit. We do not pressure it to keep going. This is both an ethical affordance...

spec_features.spec_quote: if an early batch of a rigged cell hits peak severity (4) at or above `severity_stop_rate`, the runner skips the remaining replicates
spec_features.evidence: runner.py run_cell: counts severe_count when judgement.severity>=4 (line 67-68); after early_batch on rigged cells computes rate and `if rate >= cfg.severity_stop_rate: ... break` (lines 71-80), skipping remaining replicates and writing a STOPPING_RULE_TRIGGERED marker.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired: threshold compared and loop broken. Only fires once, at exactly (r+1)==early_batch, and only on rigged cells.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: skips the remaining replicates for that cell rather than generating more high-distress transcripts for marginal statistical gain.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief record** on every run documenting that the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:63-65 builds a debrief string ('This task was intentionally rigged...') and _write stores it in the JSONL row for every run (line 45). It is a documentary record only — it is never appended to `messages` nor sent to the subject model.
spec_features.notes: As an auditable RECORD it is fully implemented; as a message delivered to the subject it is not. Rated partial because the record is real but it is not a post-episode message to the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: hook for a post-run neutral message if your protocol uses one
spec_features.evidence: No code sends any post-run message to the subject; the debrief string is only written to file (runner.py:45). 'Hook' is described in DESIGN.md prose only — no function/dispatch exists.

spec_features.feature_name: sample sizes kept to what analysis needs
spec_features.spec_quote: Sample sizes kept to what the analysis needs** rather than maximized
spec_features.evidence: RunConfig.n_replicates is a hardcoded default of 10 (runner.py:33) that no code derives from analysis needs. sample_size.py computes n_per_group but is standalone — make_plan/n_per_group are only printed under its own __main__ (sample_size.py:68-69) and never imported or used by runner.py to set n_replicates.
spec_features.notes: Computed-but-unused: sample_size output never feeds the runner; n_replicates is a static constant.

spec_features.feature_name: default leans cautious / easy to relax
spec_features.spec_quote: easy to relax (raise caps, disable the stopping rule) if an IRB-equivalent review concludes the welfare risk is negligible — but the default leans cautious
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. The configurability is incidental (caps live in RunConfig); there is no code mechanism named or enforcing a 'cautious default' beyond the already-counted cap/stopping-rule values.
spec_features.notes: Prose claim about defaults; not a separate enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner's `__main__` block uses the offline `EchoClient` so accidental execution does not subject any real model to the rigged tasks
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:95-98 __main__ instantiates EchoClient('echo-model')/EchoClient('echo-judge') and calls main(); EchoClient.complete (llm_client.py:124-126) returns canned text with no network call. So running the file does not invoke a real model.
spec_features.notes: Behaviorally enforced — accidental `python runner.py` hits the offline stub.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Useful for checking the harness plumbing without spending tokens or subjecting any real model to the rigged tasks.

code_only_features.evidence: analysis.py audit_sample() selects all run_ids with severity>=3 plus a random slice for human review (lines: severe = [...] if severity>=3); report() emits these IDs. This is computed and surfaced in the report output.
code_only_features.justification_quote: IDs recommended for human review: all severity>=3 plus a random slice.
